content.title: Objective evidence of cardiac structural, functional and serological abnormalities consistent with left ventricular diastolic dysfunction/raised LV filling pressures (Table 9)
content.intro: Notes that patients with prior overtly reduced LVEF (<40%) who later present with LVEF ≥50% should be considered to have recovered HFrEF or HF with improved LVEF rather than HFpEF; continued HFrEF treatment is recommended. Patients with HFpEF tend to have a stable LVEF trajectory but about one third may decline on follow‑up.

table_9.Parameter: LV mass index; Relative wall thickness
table_9.Threshold: LV mass index ≥95 g/m2 (female), ≥115 g/m2 (male); Relative wall thickness >0.42
table_9.Comments: Concentric LV remodelling or hypertrophy is supportive, but absence of LV hypertrophy does not exclude HFpEF.

table_9.Threshold: >34 mL/m2 (sinus rhythm); threshold >40 mL/m2 in atrial fibrillation
table_9.Comments: LA enlargement reflects chronically elevated LV filling pressure; different threshold applied in AF.
Reported sensitivity ~78% and specificity ~59% for HFpEF by invasive exercise testing; higher cut‑off (13) lowers sensitivity (~46%) but increases specificity (~86%).

table_9.Threshold: NT‑proBNP: >125 pg/mL (sinus rhythm) or >365 pg/mL (AF); BNP: >35 pg/mL (sinus rhythm) or >105 pg/mL (AF)
table_9.Comments: Up to 20% of patients with invasively proven HFpEF have natriuretic peptides below diagnostic thresholds, particularly with obesity.

table_9.Parameter: Pulmonary artery systolic pressure / TR velocity at rest
table_9.Comments: Sensitivity ~54%, specificity ~85% for presence of HFpEF by invasive exercise testing.
